nodes.label: Payment Intents
nodes.rationale: Bespoke amount calculation and PCI via Stripe.js; higher long-term maintenance than Checkout Sessions.

nodes.label: Indexes on RLS Policy Columns
nodes.rationale: Always index columns used in RLS policies so policy checks use index scans.

nodes.label: Elements with Checkout Sessions
nodes.rationale: Stripe's recommended custom-UI path: Checkout Session with ui_mode=custom, then stripe.initCheckout and Payment Element.

nodes.label: Webhook Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Process each event_id once; Stripe retries failed deliveries so handlers must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Webhook Signature Verification
nodes.rationale: Verify Stripe-Signature with the endpoint secret before handling events; reject invalid payload or signature with 400.

nodes.label: Checkout Sessions
nodes.rationale: Recommended for most integrations; hosted, embedded, or custom Elements via ui_mode=custom, with lower maintenance than Payment Intents.

nodes.label: Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.norm_label: indexes on where and join columns
nodes.rationale: Unindexed filter and join columns cause sequential scans that become exponentially slower as tables grow; index the foreign-key side of JOINs.

nodes.label: Partial Indexes
nodes.rationale: Partial indexes include only rows matching a WHERE condition, making them smaller and faster when queries consistently filter on the same predicate (soft-delete, pending status, non-null).

nodes.label: Idempotent Constraint Creation
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not support ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; migrations must check pg_constraint in a DO block before ALTER TABLE.

nodes.label: Index Foreign Key Columns
nodes.rationale: Postgres does not automatically index foreign key columns; missing indexes cause slow JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE table scans.

nodes.label: Principle of Least Privilege
nodes.rationale: Never use superuser for application queries; grant only required table/sequence privileges and revoke PUBLIC defaults so SQL injection cannot DROP everything.

nodes.label: Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: Application-only filters leak all rows on a bug or bypass; RLS enforces tenant isolation in the database, including FORCE RLS for table owners.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER Helper Functions
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS on tables it touches; always check auth.uid() inside, keep functions in a private schema, and revoke EXECUTE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role.

nodes.label: Wrap RLS Functions in SELECT
nodes.rationale: auth.uid() in a policy is invoked per row; wrapping as (select auth.uid()) caches the result once and can be 100x+ faster on large tables.

nodes.label: Helpful Content System
nodes.rationale: Site-wide signal since March 2024; thin locale translations can drag down rankings for otherwise strong pages.

nodes.label: Crawlability and Indexation
nodes.rationale: Audit priority starts with whether Google can find and index pages before technical speed, on-page, content quality, or links.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes; agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is regenerated by next dev.

nodes.label: Em Dashes as AI Tell
nodes.rationale: Models overuse em dashes as a shortcut for sentence variety because they were trained on edited books and style guides; most humans rarely type them.

nodes.label: Canonical Overrides Hreflang
nodes.rationale: If canonical points elsewhere, Google follows canonical and ignores hreflang; the canonical URL must appear in the hreflang set or all annotations are dropped. Never cross-locale canonical.

nodes.label: Next.js Sitemap Self-Reference Caveat
nodes.rationale: Next.js alternates.languages does not auto-include a self-referencing xhtml:link for the loc URL; the current locale must be added explicitly.

nodes.label: Schema Markup Detection Limitation
nodes.rationale: web_fetch and curl strip script tags and miss JS-injected JSON-LD from CMS plugins; use a browser, Google Rich Results Test, or Screaming Frog instead.

nodes.label: Create Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
nodes.norm_label: create composite indexes for multi-column queries

nodes.label: Use Covering Indexes to Avoid Table Lookups
nodes.norm_label: use covering indexes to avoid table lookups

nodes.label: BRIN Index
nodes.rationale: Use on large time-series tables; typically 10-100x smaller than B-tree.

nodes.label: B-tree Index
nodes.rationale: Default index for equality, range, BETWEEN, IN, and IS NULL; cannot optimize JSONB containment operators such as @>.

nodes.label: GIN Index
nodes.rationale: Use for arrays, JSONB, and full-text search; supports @>, ?, ?&, and ?|.

nodes.label: GiST Index
nodes.rationale: Use for geometric data, range types, and nearest-neighbor (KNN) queries.

nodes.label: Hash Index
nodes.rationale: Equality-only lookups; slightly faster than B-tree for =.

nodes.label: bigint Identity IDs
nodes.rationale: Use bigint generated always as identity rather than int, which overflows at 2.1 billion.

nodes.label: timestamptz
nodes.rationale: Always store timezone-aware timestamps; plain timestamp drops timezone info.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 Primary Keys
nodes.rationale: Time-ordered UUIDs avoid B-tree fragmentation in distributed systems; requires pg_uuidv7. ULID is an alternative without an extension.

nodes.label: Choose the Right Index Type
nodes.rationale: Different index types excel at different query patterns; the default B-tree is not always optimal and can force sequential scans for operators it does not support.

nodes.label: Appropriate PostgreSQL Data Types
nodes.rationale: Right types reduce storage, speed comparisons, and prevent bugs: bigint IDs, text not varchar(n), timestamptz, boolean, numeric for money.

nodes.label: Table Partitioning
nodes.rationale: Partition tables over ~100M rows or time-series with date filters so queries prune partitions and old data can be dropped instantly.

nodes.label: IDENTITY Primary Keys
nodes.rationale: bigint IDENTITY is SQL-standard and preferred over serial for single-database sequential IDs; better index locality and replication.

nodes.label: UUIDv4 Index Fragmentation
nodes.rationale: Random UUIDv4 primary keys scatter inserts and fragment indexes on large tables.

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications

nodes.label: Chinese Language Year
nodes.rationale: Without IELTS, TOEFL, or HSK, the realistic first step is a university Chinese-language year (汉语进修), then a Chinese-taught degree; language year and degree admission are separate files.

nodes.label: No Guarantee Policy
nodes.rationale: Do not claim the agency guarantees admission, scholarship, visa, housing, or a job; it is not a Chinese university or the CSC.

nodes.label: No Guarantee Policy
nodes.rationale: Do not claim the agency guarantees admission, scholarship, visa, housing, or a job; it is not a Chinese university or the CSC. Decisions belong to universities, scholarship bodies, and consulates.

nodes.label: Social Brand Marks
nodes.rationale: Filled #08060d wordmarks/logos for outbound social destinations (Bluesky butterfly, Discord Clyde, GitHub Octocat, X). Same fill, no stroke, brand-accurate silhouettes.

nodes.label: UI Chrome Glyphs
nodes.rationale: Unfilled rounded-stroke glyphs in #aa3bff (stroke-width 1.35): a document with code-bracket chevrons, and a person plus star. Generic chrome, not third-party brands.

nodes.label: SVG Icon Sprite Sheet
nodes.rationale: Reusable inline SVG sprite: named <symbol> icons referenced by id so the UI can <use href="#…"> without duplicating paths. Two visual families share one sheet: filled near-black brand marks versus purple-stroke UI glyphs.

nodes.label: SVG Symbol Sprite Pattern
nodes.rationale: Icons are defined as <symbol> with viewBox, not standalone files. Callers stamp a symbol by id; fill/stroke live on the paths so the sprite is a single HTTP asset.

nodes.label: Lowercase snake_case Identifiers
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase; quoted mixed-case names require quotes forever and break ORMs, tools, and AI assistants.
